question.text: Consider the augmented matrix $M$ given by \[ M= \left[\begin{array}{cc|c} 1 & -2 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 \end{array}\right]. \] Find the general solution of the linear system represented by the matrix.
question.explanation:
The system corresponding to $M$ is

\[ \left\{ \begin{array}{l} x - 2y = 1 \\ 0x+0y = 0. \end{array} \right. \]

Since any pair of numbers $x,y$ is a solution of the final equation $0x+0y = 0,$ we can remove this equation from the system. So, our system now consists of a single equation

\[ x - 2y = 1. \]

The first variable $(x)$ is the basic variable, and the second variable $(y)$ is the free variable. Solving for the basic variable $(x)$ in terms of the free variable $(y),$ we get $x=1+2y,$ and the general solution is

\[ \begin{cases} x=1 +2y \\ y=y \end{cases} \]

where $y$ is an arbitrary number.

In vector form, the general solution can be written as

\begin{align*} \begin{bmatrix}x \\ y\end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix}1 + 2y \\ y\end{bmatrix}=\langle 1+2y, \, y \rangle, \qquad y \in (-\infty,\infty). \end{align*}

question.text:
Consider the augmented matrix $M$ given by \[ M= \left[\begin{array}{cc|c} 1 & -4 & 6 \\ -2 & 8 & -12 \end{array}\right]. \]

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce $M$ to row echelon form, and then find the general solution of the linear system represented by the matrix.
question.explanation:
Reducing $M$ to echelon form, we have \begin{align*} M &= \left[\begin{array}{cc|c} 1 & -4 & 6 \\ -2 & 8 & -12 \end{array}\right] & R_2 &:= R_2 + 2R_1 \\[5pt] &\sim \left[\begin{array}{cc|c} 1 & -4 & 6 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 \end{array}\right]. \end{align*}

The corresponding system is now

\[ \left\{ \begin{array}{l} x - 4y = 6 \\ 0x+0y = 0. \end{array} \right. \]

Since any pair of numbers $x,y$ is a solution of the final equation $0x+0y = 0,$ we can remove this equation from the system. So, our system now consists of a single equation

\[ x - 4y = 6. \]

The first variable $(x)$ is the basic variable, and the second variable $(y)$ is the free variable. Solving for the basic variable $(x)$ in terms of the free variable $(y),$ we get $x=6+4y,$ and the general solution is

\[ \begin{cases} x=6 + 4y \\ y=y \end{cases} \]

where $y$ is an arbitrary number.

In vector form, the general solution can be written as \begin{align*} \begin{bmatrix}x \\ y\end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix}6 +4y \\ y\end{bmatrix}, \qquad y \in (-\infty,\infty). \end{align*}

\[ \begin{cases} x=-1-2y \\ y=y \end{cases} \]

where $y$ is an arbitrary number.

In vector form, the general solution can be written as \begin{align*} \begin{bmatrix}x \\ y\end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix}-1-2y \\ y\end{bmatrix}, \qquad y \in (-\infty,\infty). \end{align*}

question.text: Consider the system of linear equations \[ \begin{cases} x+7y = 4 \\ 6x+42y = 24. \end{cases} \] Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to row echelon form, and then find the general solution of the linear system.
question.explanation:
First, we set up the augmented matrix for the system:

\[ M = \left[\begin{array}{cc|c} 1 & 7 & 4 \\ 6 & 42 & -24 \end{array}\right] \]

Reducing $M$ to row echelon form, we have \begin{align*} M &= \left[\begin{array}{cc|c} 1 & 7 & 4 \\ 6 & 42 & 24 \end{array}\right] & R_2 &:= R_2 + (-6)R_1 \\[5pt] &\sim \left[\begin{array}{cc|c} 1 & 7 & 4 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 \end{array}\right]. \end{align*}

The corresponding system is now

\[ \left\{ \begin{array}{l} x + 7y = 4 \\ 0x+0y = 0. \end{array} \right. \]

Since any pair of numbers $x,y$ is a solution of the final equation $0x+0y = 0,$ we can remove this equation from the system. So, our system now consists of a single equation

\[ x + 7y = 4. \]

The first variable $(x)$ is the basic variable, and the second variable $(y)$ is the free variable. Solving for the basic variable $(x)$ in terms of the free variable $(y),$ we get $x=4-7y,$ and the general solution is

\[ \begin{cases} x=4 - 7y \\ y=y \end{cases} \]

where $y$ is an arbitrary number.

In vector form, the general solution can be written as \begin{align*} \begin{bmatrix}x \\ y\end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix}4 - 7y \\ y\end{bmatrix}, \qquad y \in (-\infty,\infty). \end{align*}

question.text: Consider the system of linear equations \[ \begin{cases} x-2y = -1 \\ -4x+8y = 7. \end{cases} \] Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to row echelon form, and then find the general solution of the linear system.
question.explanation:
First, we set up the augmented matrix for the system:

\[ M = \left[\begin{array}{cc|c} 1 & -2 & -1 \\ -4 & 8 & 7 \end{array}\right] \]

Reducing $M$ to row echelon form, we have

\begin{align*} M&= \left[ \begin{array}{cc|c} 1 & -2 & -1 \\ -4 & 8 & 7 \\ \end{array}\right] & R_2 &:= R_2 + 4R_1 \\[5pt] &\sim \left[\begin{array}{cc|c} 1 & -2 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & 3 \end{array}\right]. \end{align*}

The corresponding system is now \[ \left\{ \begin{array}{l} x - 2y = -1 \\ 0x+0y = 3. \end{array} \right. \]

However, the final equation $0x+0y=3$ has no solution. It simplifies to $0=3,$ which is a false statement.

So, there is no pair $x,y$ that satisfies both equations in the system. Consequently, the overall system has no solution.

question.text: Consider the system of linear equations \[ \begin{cases} 5x-10y = -5 \\ 2x- 4y = 2. \end{cases} \] Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to row echelon form, and then find the general solution of the linear system.

First, we set up the augmented matrix for the system:

\[ M = \left[\begin{array}{cc|c} 5 & -10 & -5 \\ 2 & -4 & 2 \end{array}\right] \]

Reducing $M$ to row echelon form, we have

\begin{align*} M &= \left[\begin{array}{cc|c} 5 & -10 & -5 \\ 2 & -4 & 2 \end{array}\right] & R_1 &:= \dfrac 1 5 R_1 \\[5pt] &\sim \left[\begin{array}{cc|c} 1 & -2 & -1 \\ 2 & -4 & 2 \end{array}\right] & R_2 &:= R_2 - 2R_1 \\[5pt] &\sim \left[\begin{array}{cc|c} 1 & -2 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & 4 \end{array}\right]. \end{align*}

The corresponding system is now

\[ \left\{ \begin{array}{l} x - 2y = -1 \\ 0x+0y = 4. \end{array} \right. \]

However, the final equation $0x+0y=4$ has no solution. It simplifies to $0=4,$ which is a false statement.

So, there is no pair $x,y$ that satisfies both equations in the system. Consequently, the overall system has no solution.
